title: PoE 2 Loot Filter Guide: Install, Follow and Choose Strictness
summary: How to install a PoE 2 loot filter on PC and Console, follow public filters or FilterBlade, choose the right strictness for your stage, and avoid hiding items you still need.
description: A decision-first PoE 2 loot filter guide: official follow vs FilterBlade sync vs manual file, PC/Console setup, a strictness selector, what not to hide in each stage, customisation, update and sync, and a before-use test checklist.
prerequisites: A Path of Exile account linked to your PoE 2 profile
You are drowning in drops during the campaign or early maps and want a cleaner screen
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: A pile of PoE 2 currency and item drops on the ground, the kind of loot a filter helps you sort at a glance

items.title: What is the fastest way to get a filter?
body: Follow a public filter on your Path of Exile account, then select it in-game under Options > Game > Item Filter. No file juggling required, and it works on PC and Console.

items.title: Which strictness should I start with?
body: Start loose: Regular or Semi-Strict during the campaign and early maps. Move up to Strict and Very Strict only once you stop picking up most visible drops.

items.title: Why did my drops disappear?
body: A stricter filter hides low-value items. On PC, hold Alt to reveal hidden items (their names shrink at high strictness). On Console, open the item filter panel to toggle visibility.

items.title: What should I never hide too early?
body: Currency you still use, socketed or quality gear for salvage, build-critical bases, and uniques you have not identified. Hide those only once you understand their value.

sections.title: Installation methods
sections.intro: Three ways to get a filter into PoE 2. Pick the one that matches how much control you want.

methods.name: Official account follow
steps: Open the official Path of Exile website and log in with the account you use for PoE 2.
Go to your account page, open Item Filters, then the public filter ladder.
Make sure the list is set to PoE 2, not PoE 1, before following anything.
Follow a trusted public filter such as NeverSink Regular, Semi-Strict, or Strict.
In-game, open Options > Game, find Item Filter, select the followed filter, then refresh if it does not appear.
methods.note: Cleanest hands-off method; public filters can update when the creator updates them.

methods.name: FilterBlade sync
steps: Go to filterblade.xyz and choose Path of Exile 2.
Pick a NeverSink preset strictness and customise styles, sounds, beams, and item rules.
Open the Export to PoE tab, name the filter, then Save & Sync to your account.
In-game, select the synced filter from the Item Filter dropdown and apply it.
methods.note: Best when you want control over strictness, currency tiers, and visuals while still auto-updating.

methods.name: Manual file install
steps: Download the .filter file from a trusted source.
Place it in your PoE 2 filter folder (Documents/My Games/Path of Exile 2).
In-game, use the folder icon next to the Item Filter dropdown to load the file.
Re-download and re-select whenever the filter is updated.
methods.note: Useful if you do not want to link an account, but you must update it manually.

sections.title: PC vs Console
sections.intro: The filter itself is the same. The difference is where you build it and how you toggle hidden drops.

tabs.label: PC
paragraphs: On PC you can use the official follow method, FilterBlade sync, or a manual .filter file. You also get the Alt key: hold it to reveal items hidden by the filter, and at high strictness their names shrink so they stay easy to ignore.
bullets: Full FilterBlade access with styles, sounds, and simulation.
Alt reveals hidden drops; Z toggles the whole item display.
Manual install via the Documents/My Games/Path of Exile 2 folder.

tabs.label: PlayStation / Xbox
paragraphs: Console players use the same account-linked filters but build them on a PC or web browser first, then select them in-game. There is no Alt key, so use the in-game item filter panel to check what a strict filter is hiding before you push strictness higher.
bullets: Follow or Sync a filter with your PoE account on the website, then pick it in-game.
No manual .filter file path; everything is account-linked.
Use the filter panel to preview hidden items instead of the Alt key.

sections.title: Strictness selector
sections.intro: Pick your stage and we will suggest a starting strictness and a keep list. Adjust upward only once most visible drops are things you never pick up.

rules.title: Campaign: stay loose
steps: Use Regular or Semi-Strict so you still see leveling bases, low currency, and gems.
Keep rares and uniques visible; you are still building your character.
Only hide genuinely useless items like low-level flasks and broken gear.

rules.title: Early maps: Semi-Strict
steps: Semi-Strict hides junk while showing plenty of useful items.
Highlight currency, sockets, quality, and build bases you can use or sell.
Raise strictness once your gear no longer needs random upgrades.

rules.title: Stable T15: Strict
steps: Strict is the sweet spot for consistent map farming.
It keeps value items loud and shrinks the rest.
Keep an eye on league-specific valuables before hiding them.

rules.title: Dedicated farming: Very Strict
steps: Very Strict or Uber Strict only when you know exactly what is being hidden.
Best for blasting maps where you only care about currency, high-value bases, and premium drops.
If you start missing items you need, drop strictness back down.

defaultResult.title: General rule
steps: Start simple, then make it stricter as you progress.
Never start with the strictest filter; a beginner should see more loot while learning.
Re-check hidden categories whenever your build or goals change.

sections.title: What not to hide too early
paragraphs: A filter is a tool, not a verdict on every drop. Hiding the wrong category too early can cost you upgrades, currency, or trade income. Keep these visible until you have a reason to hide them.
bullets: Currency you still use for crafting and vendor recipes, especially during the campaign.
Socketed or quality items you may want to salvage for sockets, quality, or upgrade materials.
Build-critical bases (weapon and armor types your build actually uses).
Unidentified uniques and build-required uniques; identify before judging.
Items other builds might value if you trade; do not hide whole gear categories too early.

sections.title: Customisation
paragraphs: Customisation is powerful but should be gradual. Start from a preset and change only what you understand. FilterBlade exposes every drop category so you can tune currency tiers, bases, gems, and sounds.
bullets: Campaign item progression: show bases that match your level, then stop showing outdated ones later.
Currency tiers: hide or downgrade low-value currency in endgame while making high-value drops louder.
Visual style: change text size, border color, beams, icons, and sounds if the default is too subtle or too loud.
Custom sounds: make top-tier drops obvious while keeping lower tiers quiet to avoid sound fatigue.

sections.title: Update and sync
paragraphs: Filters go stale after major patches. A filter built for one league can hide new items or miss new valuables. Keep it current.
bullets: Synced filters (official follow or FilterBlade) update when the creator publishes a new version; re-select or refresh in-game.
Manual .filter files must be re-downloaded and re-selected whenever the source updates.
After a big patch, re-open the filter editor and review tiers before pushing strictness higher.
If a followed filter has not been updated for the current patch, prefer a maintained preset.

steps.label: Confirm the game version
body: Make sure the filter is set to PoE 2, not PoE 1.
Check the filter's last update date against the current patch.

steps.label: Walk a familiar zone
body: Run a campaign or early-map zone you know well.
Verify the items you expect to see are still visible.

steps.label: Check hidden categories
body: On PC hold Alt; on Console use the filter panel to reveal what is hidden.
Confirm you are not hiding currency, bases, or uniques you still need.

steps.label: Lower strictness if unsure
body: If useful drops feel missing, drop back to Semi-Strict or Regular.
Raise strictness gradually as you learn item value.

sections.title: Community questions
sections.intro: Common loot filter questions from Reddit and video comments, with our read and a direct suggestion.

cards.title: Why did my screen suddenly go empty?
body: Problem: after switching to a strict endgame filter, almost nothing drops.
Evidence: stricter filters hide more low-value items by design.
Suggestion: you likely jumped too strict too early; drop back to Semi-Strict until you know what is hidden.

cards.title: I hid items I still needed
body: Problem: a Very Strict filter removed bases my new build wanted.
Evidence: hiding whole gear categories too early hurts multi-build accounts.
Suggestion: keep build-critical bases visible; raise strictness per category, not all at once.

cards.title: Console cannot find the filter
body: Problem: followed a filter on the website but it is missing in-game.
Evidence: console uses account-linked filters built on web/PC.
Suggestion: confirm you selected PoE 2 on the site, then refresh the in-game filter list or restart.

cards.title: Alt does not show everything
body: Problem: holding Alt still hides some names.
Evidence: at high strictness, hidden item names shrink rather than fully appear.
Suggestion: use the filter panel to inspect hidden tiers, or lower strictness for that category.

entries.label: How to Install & Customize Loot Filters for PC and Console in Path of Exile 2
entries.creator: P4wnyhof
entries.description: A practical walkthrough of installing a PoE 2 loot filter on both PC and Console, customising it, and the settings to avoid.
entries.takeaway: Follow a public filter or FilterBlade, start loose, and only raise strictness once you recognise the drops you no longer need.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: Most filter problems are version or strictness mistakes, not bugs. Read the symptoms before changing anything.
bullets: Filter missing in-game: confirm PoE 2 (not PoE 1) on the source, then refresh or restart.
Too much clutter: raise strictness one level and re-test in a known zone.
Missing useful drops: lower strictness or whitelist that category in the editor.
Sounds too noisy or too quiet: adjust alert sounds per tier in the Styles tab.
Following a PoE 1 filter: switch the ladder or preset to PoE 2 immediately.
